title: Projects
subtitle: Selected product work across healthcare, fintech, consumer platforms, and contract delivery

items.name: Tapsi Doctor Platform
items.description: Lead frontend across Tapsi Doctor’s core web products — ODoc, OMS, Physician Panel, and VMS — unifying them on Next.js 15 App Router with a shared design system, SSR where it matters, and real-time care & fulfillment flows.
items.role: Frontend Developer · Platform ownership across product surfaces
highlights: Defined a shared Next.js 15 App Router architecture — route groups, layouts, and server/client boundaries reused by ODoc, OMS, Physician Panel, and VMS
Drove the Pages Router → App Router migration with SSR/SSG strategy, dynamic segments, and route-level code splitting — ~40% faster initial loads
Established the design-system foundation (Tailwind + Headless UI) and Zustand / form / error-boundary conventions adopted across every panel
Standardized Socket.IO patterns for live order status, visit state, and patient–doctor messaging without coupling panels to each other

products.name: ODoc — Medicine ordering & online consultation
products.description: Patient-facing product for ordering medicine and booking online medical consultations — specialty discovery, physician profiles, pharmacy checkout, document upload, and live consult status.
highlights: Architected the public ODoc surface on Next.js 15 App Router with a clear server/client split: SSR/SSG for specialty & physician discovery (SEO + TTFB), client islands for checkout, consult booking, and uploads
Designed route structure for dual journeys — medicine order funnel and consultation funnel — sharing layout shells, auth gates, and design-system primitives without duplicating business UI
Implemented granular bundle splitting and streaming-friendly page composition so marketing/discovery routes stay light while transactional steps load only what they need
Integrated Socket.IO for live consultation status (queue → in-progress → completed) and aligned UI state with Zustand so patients see consistent progress across tabs and reconnects
Built resilient multi-step forms (order + consult intake) with typed validation, accessible field wiring, and error boundaries around payment and prescription-sensitive steps
Owned performance and a11y on high-traffic patient paths — focus management, keyboard flows, and reduced layout shift on SSR-hydrated discovery pages

products.name: OMS — Order panel
products.description: Internal order-management panel for pharmacy and delivery operations — order lifecycle, filters, status transitions, and high-volume fulfillment tooling used by ops day-to-day.
highlights: Led the OMS panel architecture as an authenticated App Router application — protected layouts, role-aware navigation, and isolated feature modules for order list, detail, and lifecycle actions
Built data-dense order tables and filter/search UX tuned for operator speed: predictable sorting, URL-synced query state, and progressive loading so large result sets stay responsive
Wired Socket.IO for live order-status updates so the panel reflects fulfillment changes without full refetch storms; paired with Zustand for optimistic transitions and rollback on failed mutations
Applied the same SSR shell + client-heavy workspace pattern used across internal panels — fast first paint for the authenticated chrome, deferred hydration for heavy interactive grids
Hardened reliability with typed order-domain models, centralized error boundaries around mutation-heavy flows, and consistent empty/loading/error states across the panel
Contributed to the ~40% load-time improvement by cutting unused panel chunks, lazy-loading secondary drawers/modals, and aligning caching strategy with order-list refresh patterns

products.name: Physician Panel — Doctor panel
products.description: Doctor-facing panel for running online consultations — visit queues, patient context, messaging/call flows, and clinical actions that must stay fast, clear, and accessible under time pressure.
highlights: Architected the Physician Panel as a focused clinical workspace on App Router — persistent shell for queue + active visit, with route segments for history, profile context, and consultation detail
Implemented real-time visit and messaging surfaces with Socket.IO (incoming queue, status flips, patient–doctor chat) and Zustand stores scoped per visit to avoid cross-patient state leaks
Designed UI composition for concurrent clinical work: sticky patient context, interrupt-safe status actions, and clear affordances for ending/escalating a consult without burying critical controls

Prioritized accessibility for dense clinical UI — keyboard-first queues, focus traps in dialogs, sufficient contrast, and predictable tab order so doctors can move quickly without relying on the pointer alone
Shared design-system and form primitives with ODoc/OMS while keeping physician-only domains (visit actions, clinical notes entry points) isolated behind typed module boundaries
Optimized perceived performance of the active-visit path: prefetch adjacent visit data, defer non-critical widgets, and keep the chat timeline smooth under frequent socket events

products.name: VMS — Visit management
products.description: Visit-management panel coordinating consultation lifecycle across patients, physicians, and operations — scheduling, queue health, status transitions, and cross-panel consistency with ODoc and the Physician Panel.
highlights: Modeled visit lifecycle UI on App Router with shared domain types aligned to ODoc booking and Physician Panel execution — one source of truth for status vocabulary across products
Built coordination views (queues, schedules, exception states) with real-time Socket.IO updates so ops see the same visit truth physicians and patients experience
Structured feature architecture so VMS consumes shared design-system and auth layouts while owning visit-specific modules (assignment, transitions, operational filters)
Used SSR for authenticated shell bootstrap and client rendering for live boards — balancing fast entry with continuous socket-driven updates
Introduced resilient state patterns (Zustand + explicit transition guards) to prevent illegal status jumps and to surface recoverable errors when upstream services lag
Improved operability with URL-addressable filters, consistent loading skeletons, and performance budgets on list-heavy visit boards

items.name: Nobitex Trading Experience
items.description: High-volume cryptocurrency exchange UI for Iran’s largest trading platform — real-time market data, account flows, and a shared component system tuned for heavy throughput.
highlights: Built real-time market interfaces with Socket.IO — order books, tickers, and notifications under sustained high throughput
Introduced and customized shadcn/ui as the shared component library, replacing inconsistent ad-hoc UI and accelerating feature delivery
Optimized rendering, bundle size, and asset loading — ~25% improvement in page-load times with measurable engagement lift
Led a design-pattern refactor that raised maintainability by ~35% (internal review) and shortened average bug-fix time
Partnered closely with design and product on trading and account journeys where correctness and latency both matter

items.name: Hitobit — Frontend Architecture
items.description: Contract frontend architecture work focused on performance, responsiveness, and scalable React structure for a production product surface.
highlights: Contributed to front-end architecture decisions with emphasis on maintainable module boundaries and predictable data flow
Improved perceived performance and responsiveness across key product views through render discipline and layout stability
Aligned shared UI patterns with Atomic Design conventions used across concurrent contract deliveries
Collaborated remotely with product stakeholders to ship production-ready interfaces under tight iteration cycles

items.name: Cheetavel — Next.js Foundation
items.description: Greenfield Next.js 15 App Router foundation for a scalable product — routing architecture, Atomic Design structure, and a shadcn/ui-based design system from day one.
highlights: Designed and implemented the foundational Next.js v15 architecture using the App Router for optimized routing and long-term scalability
Established Atomic Design component structure so feature teams can compose UI without duplicating primitives
Adopted shadcn/ui + Zustand as the baseline design-system and state stack for greenfield velocity
Set conventions for forms (React Hook Form), real-time hooks (Socket.IO-ready), and folder boundaries that scale with the product

items.name: Pool Khord — Cross-platform UI
items.description: End-to-end product UI across React Native, React, and Next.js — shared visual language, responsive Tailwind layouts, and form patterns that travel between mobile and web.
highlights: Delivered comprehensive UI across React Native, React, and Next.js while keeping interaction patterns consistent for users
Implemented responsive Tailwind layouts that adapt cleanly from mobile-first flows to desktop density
Used React Hook Form for typed, reusable validation across multi-step and high-interaction forms
Shared Atomic Design primitives and Zustand/Recoil state patterns with sibling contract products for faster delivery

items.name: Axon — Web Product Surfaces
items.description: Responsive React applications and CMS-driven marketing surfaces — Redux state, SEO collaboration, and modular CSS architecture that sped delivery across product initiatives.
highlights: Owned dynamic landing pages and content-management surfaces; partnered with SEO to remove handoff friction between teams
Implemented BEM methodology for modular CSS — ~20% faster delivery and fewer style regressions
Built production interfaces with Tailwind CSS, Bootstrap, and Vuetify across concurrent product initiatives
Collaborated with cross-functional teams on Redux-based state and performance-conscious responsive layouts
